body: U.S. cybersecurity agency CISA has confirmed that hackers are now actively exploiting a pair of critical security vulnerabilities in the widely used PHP web software and has ordered civilian federal agencies within the U.S. government to fix their systems within the next three days. [...] While the bugs are rated critical, meaning they can be highly damaging if exploited, security researchers said that developing a working exploit to hack into vulnerable systems was initially challenging — but not impossible. Confirmed in-the-wild exploitation now puts extra pressure on organizations to patch their systems to prevent malicious compromises, disruption, and data breaches. [...] The two bugs in PHP are among countless vulnerabilities that have not yet been discovered or have been deprioritized for years but now pose a risk due to advances in AI models’ ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities, including by chaining multiple flaws together.

title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware threatens most servers on planet Earth - Ars Technica
body: The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot, which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. While final payloads delivered by CVE-2026-97631 have no persistence—meaning they run only once—they can give attackers a wide opening to install [...] There are important caveats and limitations to exploiting this latest vulnerability. As noted, some level of control over a local network is a prerequisite. That likely limits exploitation to insiders or attackers, such as nation-states or ransomware operators, who manage to gain low-level access inside a network and are looking for a way to elevate system rights. There’s no evidence yet that CVE-2026-97631 provides an initial entry point into a network. There are other hurdles to clear. [...] CVE-2026-97631 joins a long list of previously discovered vulnerabilities in UEFI or code that works closely with it. The most severe of them, LogoFail, stemmed from logo images included in the UEFI of just about every hardware maker. Rendering bugs allowed attackers to subvert the chain of trust UEFI enforces and go on to install malicious components before the OS loaded or Secure Boot ran. PixieFail was a vulnerability similar to CVE-2026-97631. It, too, was the result of faulty PXE boot

[...] Beyond technical bottlenecks, Miller contended that the semiconductor landscape is being reshaped by the demands of global political leaders seeking to align supply chains with their own national interests. Miller previously traced this power struggle in his 2022 New York Times bestseller, Chip War, which underscores how control over computing power has historically dictated military and economic advantage. This trend has only intensified in 2026, as evidenced by the rising use of tariffs and [...] What makes this technology unique, Miller argued, is a reliance on supply chains that—for the first time in history—cannot be managed by a single nation. Instead, these goods are produced across multiple countries and continents. “Today there's not a single country in the world that can produce, not even an advanced chip, but a moderately advanced chip on its own,” he said. title: Anthropic nets $15B from Nvidia and Microsoft as AI bets overlap - PitchBook
body: # Anthropic nets $15B from Nvidia and Microsoft as AI bets overlap Microsoft and Nvidia are investing up to $15 billion in a newly announced partnership with OpenAI competitor Anthropic. The partnership includes a commitment from Anthropic to purchase $30 billion in Microsoft Azure compute credits and up to a gigawatt of compute capacity powered by Nvidia chips. But the announcement also notes that Amazon, which has invested $8 billion into the company, will remain Anthropic’s primary cloud provider. The deal highlights how investors in OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI aren’t taking sides over the future of generative AI, with many backing at least two out of the three—or now, in Nvidia’s case, investing in all three.

title: Anthropic to buy $30 billion in Azure capacity in new deal with Microsoft, Nvidia - CNBC
body: # Anthropic to buy $30 billion in Azure capacity in new deal with Microsoft, Nvidia * Microsoft announced new strategic partnerships with Nvidia and the AI startup Anthropic. Microsoft will invest $5 billion into Anthropic, while Nvidia will invest $10 billion into the startup. * Microsoft has also invested billions of dollars into Anthropic's rival OpenAI. Microsoft on Tuesday announced new strategic partnerships with Nvidia and the artificial intelligence startup Anthropic, the latest sign that the company is working to reduce its dependence on OpenAI. As part of the agreement, Microsoft will invest $5 billion into Anthropic, while Nvidia will invest $10 billion into the startup. Microsoft has invested billions of dollars into Anthropic's rival OpenAI, backing the company as early as 2019.

title: Tech giants pour billions into Anthropic as circular AI investments roll on - Ars Technica
body: ChatGPT competitor secures billions from Microsoft and Nvidia in deal to use cloud services and chips. On Tuesday, Microsoft and Nvidia announced plans to invest in Anthropic under a new partnership that includes a $30 billion commitment by the Claude maker to use Microsoft’s cloud services. Nvidia will commit up to $10 billion to Anthropic and Microsoft up to $5 billion, with both companies investing in Anthropic’s next funding round. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said in a video that OpenAI “remains a critical partner,” while adding that the companies will increasingly be customers of each other. OpenAI has since announced a $38 billion deal to buy cloud services from Amazon.com as the company becomes less dependent on Microsoft.

title: Pentagon strikes classified AI deals with OpenAI, Google, and Nvidia — but not Anthropic - The Verge
body: # Pentagon strikes classified AI deals with OpenAI, Google, and Nvidia — but not Anthropic. The flurry of deals leaves out Anthropic, which the department previously used for handling classified information. The flurry of deals leaves out Anthropic, which the department previously used for handling classified information. The Pentagon has struck deals with OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, Elon Musk’s xAI, and the startup Reflection, allowing the agency to use their AI tools in classified settings, according to an announcement on Friday. This builds upon deals with OpenAI and xAI, which have already reached agreements with the Pentagon for the “lawful” use of their AI systems. And while Anthropic had a $200 million deal to handle classified materials for the Pentagon, it refused to loosen “red lines” around mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons for the agency, leading to a dispute that banned the AI startup’s products from the federal government. * Google and Pentagon reportedly agree on deal for ‘any lawful’ use of AI.

title: There Is Only One AI Company. Welcome to the Blob - WIRED
body: As Nvidia, OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft forge partnerships and deals, the AI industry is looking more like one interconnected machine. Microsoft’s press release sums it up in three lines, like a subpar Allen Ginsberg verse: “Anthropic to scale Claude on Azure / Anthropic to adopt NVIDIA architecture / NVIDIA and Microsoft to invest in Anthropic.” The deal has the earmarks of what critics call a circular arrangement, whereby money goes back and forth between companies before a single customer is involved. Anthropic doesn’t have its own cloud or a non-AI-related revenue flow like Google, Microsoft, or Meta, so it’s now added Microsoft to its previous stock-for-compute deals with Amazon and Google.
